html:
A church council held at Nicaea in 787 that restored the use of holy images, icons, and ended the first period of Byzantine iconoclasm. It is the seventh and last council recognised as ecumenical by both the Orthodox and Catholic churches.

Since the 720s emperors had banned icons as idolatry. Empress Irene, ruling for her young son Constantine VI, wanted them back. A first attempt to meet in Constantinople in 786 was broken up by soldiers loyal to iconoclasm, so the bishops met the next year in Nicaea, the city of the first council in 325.

The council ruled that icons may be honoured with veneration, which passes to the person shown, but that worship belongs to God alone. Iconoclasm returned in 815 and was ended for good in 843, under the Empress Theodora. In the West, Charlemagne's court, working from a poor Latin translation, rejected the council's decrees.
sum: A church council held at Nicaea in 787 that restored the use of holy images, icons, and ended the first period of Byzantine iconoclasm. It is the seventh and last council recognised as ecumenical by both the Orthodox and Catholic churches.
